subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 3-year-old boy is evaluated for progressive spasticity and toe-walking, and he has mild intellectual disability. Plasma arginine is markedly elevated and ammonia is only mildly increased; he has had no episodes of acute encephalopathy. Plasma argininosuccinate and urine orotic acid are normal.
question: Deficiency of which enzyme is most likely?
explanation_correct: Arginase hydrolyzes arginine to urea and ornithine; its deficiency, called hyperargininemia, causes marked elevation of plasma arginine with progressive spastic diplegia and intellectual disability. Hyperammonemia is usually less severe and less acute than in proximal urea cycle defects.

explanation_incorrect.A: Argininosuccinate lyase deficiency raises argininosuccinate and causes acute neonatal hyperammonemia.
explanation_incorrect.B: Ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency is X-linked, causes orotic aciduria, and typically presents with acute hyperammonemia.
explanation_incorrect.D: Argininosuccinate synthetase deficiency raises citrulline and causes marked hyperammonemia.
explanation_incorrect.E: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I deficiency presents in the neonatal period with severe hyperammonemia and low citrulline.

educationalObjective: Arginase deficiency causes hyperargininemia with progressive spastic diplegia and less severe hyperammonemia than proximal urea cycle defects.
